newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: France's Vasseur urges zero EU farm set-aside.
newsitem.headline: France's Vasseur urges zero EU farm set-aside.

text.p: French Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur on Monday called for cereals set-aside to be fixed at a zero rate for the 1998 harvest.
"I consider that only a zero set-aside rate can meet Europe's objectives," Vasseur told a meeting of European Union farm ministers.
Vasseur said that it was of the utmost priority for France that the set-aside rate is agreed as part of the 1997/98 farm price package and at the latest by June 30, 1997.
The cereals market situation is causing concern, he said, noting that stocks were too low to allow good management of prices.
"Frost in the United States and drought in Europe will not improve matters," he added.
If set-aside had been reduced to zero for the 1977 harvest -- instead of being halved to five percent -- no-one would be talking about possible wheat export taxes, he said.

Vasseur called for the abolition of penalty set-aside, whereby farmers have to take extra land out of production if they exceed planting limits, saying that member states were unable to apply the penalties in a uniform and coherent manner.
Vasseur also reiterated strong French opposition to proposals to cut cereals and oilseed area aid and set-aside payments.
The European Commission has proposed cuts amounting to 1.4 billion ecus in a move to help fund aid for beef producers hit by the mad cow crisis.
"Such a decision would unbalance the 1992 reform of the Common Agricultural Policy without offering any medium term opportunities for European agriculture," he said.
